To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new efficient method has been developed for the simulation of the extreme response values of offshore structures which can be used for a wide range of sea states.
a new efficient time simulation method is proposed for the prediction of the probability distribution of response extreme values of offshore structures.
the correlation between the response and surface elevation extreme values reduces with the intensity of the sea state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a more efficient and accurate method for predicting the probability distributions of extreme values of response of offshore structures.
the derivation of the probability distribution of extreme response by efficient time simulation method.
the development of efficient simulation techniques for predicting the probability distributions of extreme values of offshore structural response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ETS technique can be used to efficiently predict the probability distribution of response extreme values for a wide range of sea states, provided that the correlation between response and surface elevation extreme values is sufficiently large.
the ETS technique has the potential to reduce the sampling variance by a factor of about 10 for high-intensity wave loading and by a factor of 1000 for low-intensity wave loading.
for sea states of high intensity, the ETS technique with linear response values (ETS-L) is recommended, while for sea states of low intensity, the CTS is recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the new technique is more efficient and hence more accurate than the CTS technique for a large range of sea state intensities, while the ETS technique remains the more efficient technique in the case of high-intensity sea-states.
the ETS method can be used to predict the probability distribution of response extreme values in a wide range of wave conditions.
the ETS technique can be used for the efficient prediction of the probability distribution of offshore response extremes for sea states of high intensity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ETS technique can be used to predict the probability distribution of response extreme values in a very efficient and accurate manner for both high and low intensity sea states.

for sea states of low intensity, the correlation between the nonlinear response and the linear response extreme values is higher than that between the surface elevation and nonlinear response extreme values and therefore the former correlation should be used for predicting the distribution of the extreme value of nonlinear response.
the correlation between the linear and the nonlinear response extreme values is more significant than the correlation between the surface elevation and the nonlinear response.
